cues.text: Section one.
What is IT strategy?
IT strategy is a long-term plan for using technology, people, processes and information to achieve organisational objectives.
A good strategy explains why investments are necessary, what capabilities must be built, who is accountable, how delivery will occur, and how success will be measured.
It is important to see what a strategy is not.
Buying servers, hiring programmers or moving to the cloud is not itself a strategy.
Those are possible means to an end, not the end itself.
Let us consider an example.
Imagine a Nigerian retailer that is experiencing stockouts.
Its business goal is to increase sales by improving product availability.
An appropriate IT strategy here would integrate point-of-sale data with inventory records and demand forecasting.
Now compare that with a proposal to replace every computer with a newer model.
That proposal may be technically attractive, but it does not necessarily solve the problem of stockouts.
Next, we need to separate four related ideas.
Mission describes the organisation's purpose.
Vision describes its desired future.
Strategic objectives specify the results needed to reach that future.
And IT objectives translate those results into technology-enabled capabilities.
To make this concrete, the source gives a table with three columns: business objective, IT capability, and measure.
Let us go through it row by row.
In the first row, the business objective is to improve customer retention.
The IT capability is a CRM, together with personalised service.
The measure is the repeat purchase rate.
In the second row, the business objective is to reduce claims delays.
The IT capability is an automated claims workflow.
The measure is the median processing time.
In the third row, the business objective is to expand geographically.
The IT capability is scalable cloud and mobile services.
The measure is the number of new customers served.
In the fourth row, the business objective is to reduce fraud.
The IT capability is transaction monitoring.
The measure is fraud loss and the false-positive rate.
Notice the pattern across all four rows.
Each starts with a business need, then names the technology capability that supports it, and finally states how we will measure whether it worked.
Finally, what makes a strategy good?
A good strategy is forward-looking, business-focused, measurable, practical, iterative, and developed with stakeholders.
When done well, it enables innovation, reduces unnecessary expenditure, improves customer experience, mitigates risk, and increases adaptability.
